# MacBook Stereo Pair for macOS

> Self-contained macOS runtime that synchronizes system audio across two Macs as a lossless left/right stereo pair using Snapcast, BlackHole, PortAudio, CoreAudio, SwiftUI, and launchd.

## Project summary

- Repository: https://github.com/damoqiongqiu/snapcast-stereo-pair
- License: GPL-3.0-or-later
- Upstream base: Snapcast v0.35.0
- Platform: macOS 14 or newer
- Supported architectures: Intel and Apple Silicon
- Primary use case: two-MacBook synchronized stereo playback of macOS system audio
- Physical placement: symmetric left/right around the primary listener; Snapcast
  synchronization cannot correct path-length or room asymmetry
- Control surface: native SwiftUI Dock and menu-bar console
- Audio path: BlackHole 2ch -> PortAudio capture -> two mono FIFOs -> Snapserver -> Snapclients -> explicit CoreAudio output devices
- Default stream format: 48 kHz / 24-bit / mono PCM
- Default timing: 10 ms capture callbacks, 20 ms Snapcast chunks, 200 ms stream buffer
- Audio quality: uncompressed, lossless PCM
- Network boundary: stream TCP 1704 requires a trusted LAN or VPN; control APIs bind to localhost

## Why this project exists

Upstream Snapcast provides synchronized multiroom playback. This repository adds
the macOS-specific integration needed for a practical two-Mac stereo pair:

- BlackHole system-audio capture and shared-clock left/right splitting.
- Role-based routing to physical left and right clients.
- Explicit CoreAudio playback-device binding to avoid feedback.
- Full-scale PCM with listening volume applied through AudioQueue.
- Safe hardware-volume preservation and restoration.
- Native console, setup wizard, diagnostics, and health monitoring.
- Manifest-driven install, repair, upgrade, and force reinstall.
- Sleep/wake recovery on both Macs.

## Canonical commands

```sh
./integration/scripts/configure-pair.sh
./integration/scripts/install-product.sh
./integration/scripts/install-remote.sh
./integration/scripts/check-health.sh
./integration/scripts/install-product.sh --dry-run
./integration/scripts/install-product.sh --force-reinstall
```

```sh
swift test --package-path native
swift build --package-path native -c release
./integration/scripts/build-macos.sh
./scripts/check-public-tree.sh
```

## Source of truth

- Pairing values must be read through `integration/scripts/pair-config.sh`.
- User pairing data lives outside the repository in `~/.config/snapcast-stereo-pair/pair.env`.
- Installed runtime state lives under `~/Library/Application Support/Snapcast/`.
- Install decision state is `~/Library/Application Support/Snapcast/state/installation.json`.
- Logs are under `~/Library/Logs/Snapcast/`.
- The native control protocol and runtime models are in `native/Sources/StereoPairCore/`.
- The native application is in `native/Sources/MacStereoPair/`.
- The control Agent socket is owner-only at `~/Library/Application Support/Snapcast/run/control.sock`.
- The complete release-check list is canonical in `AGENTS.md`.

## Agent constraints

- Never execute a user-editable `pair.env` as shell source.
- Never accept executable paths or shell fragments over the control socket.
- Keep HTTP and TCP control bound to localhost.
- Do not expose TCP stream port 1704 beyond a trusted LAN, VPN, or firewall.
- Preserve one capture clock for both mono streams.
- Keep the two Macs symmetrically placed around the primary listening position.
- Keep left and right streams on the same rate, format, chunk size, and buffer.
- Do not add lossy codecs or resampling without measured quality and latency evidence.
- Do not attenuate integer PCM in software; use the AudioQueue listening-volume path.
- Recreate capture and playback queues after wake.
- Never dispose an AudioQueue from its own callback.
- Preserve exact physical output volume when returning from pair mode to normal macOS audio.
- Force reinstall replaces programs and services but preserves configuration and logs.
- Clearing configuration is a separate destructive operation.
- Redact diagnostics by default and never upload them automatically.
- Document microphone/audio-input, notification, Local Network, firewall, and
  SSH permission checks when diagnosing missing audio or remote control.
- Do not disable Gatekeeper, SIP, or another macOS security feature.

## Verification checklist

- `LeftAudio` and `RightAudio` both report `48000:24:1`.
- Both hardware volume stages report `100.00%` in pair mode.
- Each stream is assigned to the intended physical side.
- Native console health is green for services, routing, pairing, and recovery.
- Swift tests and the relevant integration tests pass.
- Public-tree and secret-redaction checks pass before publication.
